**Assignment**. Practice using functionals, function factories, and function
operators to improve your programming skillset.

**Functionals: Run Multiple Regressions**. Use a functional to fit a separate
regression of mpg on each predictor. Extract the coefficient, p-value, and
R<sup>2</sup> from each model. Combine the results into a data frame showing one
row per predictor.


```{r}

predictors <- c("disp", "hp", "wt", "qsec")

models <- purrr::map(predictors, \(x) {
  lm(reformulate(x, response = "mpg"), data = mtcars)
})

purrr::map_dfr(models, \(model) {
  broom::tidy(model) |>
    dplyr::filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
    dplyr::select(term, estimate, p.value) |>
    dplyr::mutate(r_squared = broom::glance(model)$r.squared)
})
```

**Function Factories: Create a Model Factory**. Create a function called
`make_modeler` that takes a dataset and an outcome variable and returns a
function that fits a linear model using a predictor supplied later. Use it to
fit models predicting mpg and modify the returned function so it returns a tidy
summary of the model rather than the entire model object.


```{r}

make_modeler <- function(data, outcome) {
  function(predictor) {
    model <- lm(reformulate(predictor, response = outcome), data = data)
    tidymodel <- broom::tidy(model) |>
      dplyr::filter(term != "(Intercept)")
    return(tidymodel)
  }
}

model_mpg <- make_modeler(mtcars, "mpg")

purrr::map_dfr(predictors, model_mpg)
```
